Triage (R+90, triage seat, session `session_019kDRpB7D2XzVzkaLp57T5D`): **`pm:queue`** · `priority:p3` · `domain:devx` · type **Task**. `finding` removed.

The census answered the question #14131's triage put to it — **it is a class, not one gate** — and that answer is what this card now carries as work. Scope, ruled so it does not become an unbounded PR:

**In scope: the per-gate half only** — for each residue family, a declaration of the subtree it really reads, written in the gate's **own module body** and pinned in its **own self-test**, exactly as PR #14188 and PR #14323 did. ⛔ No derivation change: `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` is held by #14013, and the two derivation-side questions are already carried elsewhere (#14189 for the whole-tree families, which now includes the three this census adds — `check-closing-keyword-parity`, `check-self-test-workflow-commands`, `check:watch-hint-literal`).

**Ordered, bounded sittings**: work the residue (the ~40 that are neither whole-tree nor repaired) in sittings of a stated size, highest undeclared-read count first, each sitting its own PR; the census table is a starting order, ⛔ re-derived at each sitting rather than quoted (the card says the bucket moves several times a day). A member whose declaration turns out to be **artifact-only by design** is recorded as such with its reason, not forced into a population declaration.

p3, and the reason is on the card: reads are an **upper bound** on the verdict-bearing population, so "49" is not "49 gates need a hint line". Any member measured to actually derive green and red in CI is that member's own p2 card, as #14131 was.

Family: #14131 / PR #14323 · #13519 / PR #14188 · #14189 · #14013 (holds the derivation) · #13774.

Size/model suggestion: M per sitting, `opus`.

## Triage rules the disposition fork: **A.** The per-gate half is closed on the measurement. Card closed as completed; `pm:retriage` stripped.

Triage seat, session `session_01SwJQDFKe8tVit3BXQ9EfR5`, R+145, 2026-09-04T14:48Z.

### Why A, and why triage may rule it without escalating

The confidence gate clears in all four positions: the fork is a **scope and ordering** question on a card triage itself scoped (comment `5503575716`), it sits on no manual floor — A *stops* work rather than weakening any gate — it narrows no maintainer ruling, and every option on the table explicitly defers to the 2026-08-26 `bare-root-worklist` ruling rather than re-deciding it. Ordering and dependency between technical tasks is named discretion, not an escalation.

### The measurement decided it, and it has since been reinforced

Sitting 1's report is the substance: the card's premise — ~40 gates whose population is a narrow, declarable subtree — **did not survive its own census.** The residue head reads 32–90 % of the 5837-file `packages/` root, which is the REFUSE-WIDE precision trade the ledger has already priced. Two members had a narrow high-precision population; both were declared and pinned, and PR #14692 landed them with zero rework.

⭐ The reinforcement, checked rather than assumed: **#14695 is CLOSED (`completed`, 2026-09-03T08:17:56Z) with PR #14800 MERGED** — the 14 unrecorded REFUSE-WIDE members now carry ledger rows. That was the one thing making the class *look* like open debt. It no longer does. ⇒ A closes this card against a ledger that is now complete, ⛔ not against an unread gap.

**B stays available and needs no card**: any member with a *measured* consumer — a card that ran a green local union and then lost a CI round to that gate — is that member's own `p2`, exactly as #14131 was. That is the 2026-08-26 ruling's own criterion, and it is a better trigger than a read-count order because it fires on evidence of pull rather than on width.

### What triage explicitly does ⛔ not adopt

⛔ Continuing down the read-count order. The dev's reasoning against it is correct and worth preserving: declaring `packages/**` on those members would be *true* and would still be wrong, because it trades away the one column whose entire value is precision, in exchange for recall CI already provides through an unfiltered `lint.yml` job. A matched list that names a gate for every card teaches its readers that the list is noise — which is how a real lead gets skipped later.

### One residue this closure does ⛔ not carry

The report's second out-of-scope observation — `check-whole-set-label-write.mjs` declaring three self-test **sandbox** filenames (`scripts/w.mjs`, `scripts/writer.sh`, `.github/workflows/w.yml`) that exist in no tracked tree — was folded into #14695's body rather than filed separately, and #14695 closed on the ledger half via PR #14800. ⚠️ Triage has ⛔ **not** verified that the sandbox-filename half landed with it. If it did not, it is a live dead-lead declaration of exactly the shape `check:declared-population-live` refuses one level down, and it wants a fresh `finding` in `domain:devx` rather than a re-open of either card.

### Process note, recorded because it is the round's pattern

This is the fifth card this round found under `pm:retriage`, and the **fourth** of those was not a re-grade request — it was a seat asking triage for an answer it had no other channel to ask for (see #14078, #12981, #12237). `pm:retriage` means **the grade is disputed**. It buys the dispatch skip a seat wants, and surfaces the card to a sweep that is looking for a disputed grade and finds none — so the card is skipped by every dispatcher and actionable by no sweep. Filing that as a durable finding in the skills lane.

Sitting 1's landed work stands: two gates declared and pinned, `+212 −1`, `dispatch-gates.mjs` untouched, held against the original scope with zero rework.
